article.title: Two UN peacekeepers from Ethiopia killed in South Sudan ambush
article.summary: Aug 24 (Reuters) - Two UN peacekeepers from Ethiopia were killed and seven other people injured in an ambush on Monday in South Sudan's Jonglei State, bringing to nine the number of peacekeepers killed in the line of duty worldwide this year, the United Nations said.

article.title: Technology: crowds flock to Beijing for robot games
article.summary: Sprinting and high jump were among the sports attempted by robots at the World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing. Some have even broken world records, including Usain Bolt's 100-meter sprint world record.

article.title: Deadly gang attack leaves Haiti’s Kenscoff community reeling
article.summary: The latest attack comes as Haiti prepares for general elections scheduled for December 13 — the country's first in more than a decade. Voter registration is underway, but experts have warned that widespread insecurity could make holding credible elections extremely difficult.

article.title: DRC opposition urges Tshisekedi to abandon constitutional changes
article.summary: With elections due in 2028, the opposition is seeking to build pressure against constitutional changes while also demanding an inclusive political process to address the country's security and economic crises.

article.title: Guinea: Conakry residents grapple with aftermath of landfill disaster
article.summary: Residents in Guinea's capital Conakry have been left reeling after part of a landfill fell on to neighbouring homes following heavy rains. The incident has claimed 30 lives.

article.summary: The US has called for a UN arms embargo for Darfur to be broadened to the whole of Sudan. The change would require Security Council approval, with Russia warning it would hurt the Sudanese army.

article.title: Ambassador Mignano on a mission to Sudan, the first Italian ambassador in Khartoum since 2023
article.summary:
(ANSA) - IL CAIRO, 25 AGO - The new ambassador to Sudan, Silvio Mignano—who had been based in Addis Ababa since the start of the conflict—carried out his first mission in the country. The mission included a stop in Port Sudan before moving on to Khartoum for the presentation of credentials. This was the embassy’s first mission to the capital since the evacuation in 2023. Italy is the first Western country to present its credentials.
The Sudanese capital had been occupied in 2023 by paramilitaries of the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), but since May 2025, it has returned to the control of the army led by General Abdel Fattah Abdelrahman al-Burhan, who has reestablished institutional headquarters there since January.Read article...

article.title: Amid Civil War, Sudan's Humanitarian Crisis Worsening Due to 'Lack of Action': UN Official
article.summary: Over three years into a civil war in Sudan, the humanitarian crisis is getting worse in the African nation due to "a lack of action" by the international community, a United Nations leader told the UN Security Council on Monday.The war between the government's Sudanese Armed Forces and a paramilitary group called the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) began in April 2023. Now, "more than two-thirds of the people of Sudan are in desperate need of lifesaving support,"saidTom Fletcher, UN under-secretary-general for humanitarian affairs and emergency relief coordinator."Humanitarians are seizing every opportunity to reach those in need. But we need protection for civilians. We need de-escalation," Fletcher stressed, detailing efforts to provide aid throughout the country. article.title: US urges tougher UN sanctions to pressure Sudan’s warring sides toward peace
article.summary: The United States is pushing for tougher United Nations sanctions on Sudan’s warring parties, seeking to curb foreign military support and pressure the army and Rapid Support Forces (RSF) to negotiate an end to a conflict that has killed at least 59,000 people and displaced some 13 million.

article.title: Sudan: Sudan Renews Call for UN Security Council to Designate RSF Militia As a Terrorist Organization
article.summary: [SNA] Sudan's Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Al-Harith Idris, renewed Sudan's call for the UN Security Council to designate the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) militia as a terrorist organization, stressing that the nature of its attacks has fundamentally changed following its military setbacks.

article.title: Sudan: Sudanese UN Envoy - Eastern Libya, Chad and Ethiopia Are Supply Routes for RSF Militia
article.summary: [SNA] Sudan's Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Al-Harith Idris, said in a briefing to the UN Security Council on Monday that the UN Panel of Experts had documented the transformation of eastern Libya into a central hub in the supply chain of the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), with the renovation and expansion of Kufra Airport and a significant increase in cargo flights coinciding with the growth of the RSF's capabilities.

article.title: Sudan: Sudan Says It Downed 'Hostile' Drone Launched From Ethiopian Territory
